source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 29:31 ('וירא ה׳ כי שנואה — the final letters spell אהיה: because she was suspected, the Holy One set His own name upon her as witness')
claim_en: THE NAME IN THE FINALS: the four words 'and YHWH SAW that hated...' (29:31) end in the letters of אהיה ('I WILL BE' — the bush-Name), in order: the Kitzur reads God signing His witness on the suspected wife in the verse's own last letters, at the verse that opens her womb.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:31 ('the Ramah: שנואה written FULL with vav, and all the Torah likewise full, except ONE written with yod and read with chirik — and-the-firstborn-shall-be TO THE HATED')
claim_en: THE HATED-WORD RUNS FULL: שנואה ('hated') in its bare form stands three times in the Torah, all vav-full as the Ramah rules — Leah's two tokens (29:31, 29:33) and the hated-wife law's own opening ('the one loved and the one HATED,' Deut 21:15).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:31 (the Ramah's exception clause)
claim_en: AND THE LAW'S ONE YOD: the single exception is לשניאה — written with YOD — at Deut 21:15's own climax: 'the firstborn shall be TO THE HATED one.' The law that guards the hated wife's firstborn (the Leah-and-Reuben case, verse for verse) spells her word differently at exactly the clause that protects her son: one letter apart, as the Ramah counts it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:35 ('ותעמד — lean, no vav; the Ramah: every stand-form of this shape in the Torah is written lean')
claim_en: THE CESSATION WRITTEN LEAN: ותעמד ('and she STOOD from bearing,' 29:35 — the pause after Judah) — defective as ruled, the form's only Torah token, and no full-spelled twin exists anywhere in the Torah: the Ramah's all-lean rule holds whole.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 29:34 ('קרא שמו — the meteg on the qof in the precise manuscripts')
claim_en: THE WITHHELD NAMER'S OWN STROKE: קרא ('he CALLED his name Levi,' 29:34 — the twelve writes' one masculine naming-verb, its subject withheld by the letter) carries the meteg (the small stress-stroke) of the precise manuscripts and the maqqef joining it to the name-word — as Minchat Shai rules, on the one naming the machine could not assign.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:3 ('ותלד על ברכי — Minchat Kohen wrote the kaf soft, and his words are bewildering: in ALL the books the kaf is dageshed, and the Masorah rules every knee-word dageshed except two soft ones — in Judges and in Daniel')
claim_en: THE KNEES AS RULED: ברכי ('that she may bear UPON MY KNEES,' 30:3 — the adoptive-birth formula) — kaf with dagesh (the doubling dot) per all the books, Minchat Kohen's soft reading refuted; the Masorah's two soft knee-words (Gideon's kneelers, Daniel's kneeling) are both outside the Torah, named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:6 ('דנני — the second nun dageshed; the Masorah: THERE IS NO DAGESH LIKE IT; the Michlol explains it as compensating the assimilated nun, and some say it is for adornment — and that is the correct view')
claim_en: THE ONE-OF-A-KIND DAGESH AT DAN: דנני ('God has JUDGED ME,' 30:6 — Dan's etiology) — the second nun dageshed, and the Masorah marks the dagesh itself as one of a kind ('there is none like it'): the judge-name is born on a doubling the tradition counts unique, adornment by the ruling Minchat Shai endorses.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:7 ('בן שני ליעקב — the bet in tzere in the precise books and WITHOUT maqqef; the Great Scriptures' maqqef is an error — the every-joined-son-takes-segol rule belongs to the sixth-son verse, as the Masorah itself says')
claim_en: THE SECOND SON UNJOINED: בן ('a second SON to Jacob,' 30:7) — bet in tzere (the long e) with NO maqqef, per the precise books; the printed maqqef-plus-segol reading is the error Minchat Shai dismantles, its rule belonging to another verse. SNAPSHOT letter-identical with the precise camp.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:8 ('אלהים — with paseq')
claim_en: THE PASEQ OF THE WRESTLINGS (manual): Minchat Shai rules a paseq (the separating bar) after אלהים in 'wrestlings of God I have wrestled' (30:8, Naphtali's etiology); the paseq layer is absent from SNAPSHOT's stream (builder-probed: no separator in the verse) — the standing gap's second source-anchored instance, after the run-5 probe.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:11 ('בגד — written one word and lacking aleph, read TWO: בא גד; the Ramah counts it among the FIFTEEN words written one and read two, the list preserved at Chronicles; see the Zohar at Vayechi')
claim_en: WRITTEN ONE, READ TWO — INSIDE A NAME: at Gad's etiology (30:11) the WRITTEN form stands as one bare unpointed word beside the READ pair 'FORTUNE HAS COME' — two pointed tokens — exactly the fifteen-list's encoding, carried natively by SNAPSHOT's written/read token-pairing: the corpus's first such pair inside a name-etiology, chain-attested to the Ramah's fifteen.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:16 ('מן השדה — with meteg and with maqqef')
claim_en: FROM THE FIELD, JOINED: מן before the field-word ('and Jacob came FROM THE FIELD at evening,' 30:16) carries the maqqef (the joining stroke) as ruled; the meteg (the lengthening stroke) the ruling adds is NOT in the stream — the meteg-omission class takes another member (variance note, with the join itself verified).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:16 ('בלילה הוא — one of the FOUR the Masorah lists as expected-THAT read-IT, the list preserved at Vayera')
claim_en: THE NIGHT THE LETTER LEAVES BARE: הוא in 'he lay with her THAT night' (30:16) — the sense expects the the-prefixed form; the letter writes the bare word, one of the Masorah's FOUR such night-stations (the Vayera list, named): the expected-form class (the run-4 sevirin family) takes its in-span member on the mandrake night.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:18 ('יששכר — the whole Torah writes TWO shins and ONE is read, by Ben Asher's reading; the Ramah, Ibn Ezra at the head of Exodus, and the Radak's Michlol with its doubled-letter parallels; R. Elia's dissent quoted')
claim_en: THE NAME WITH THE SILENT LETTER: יששכר ('Issachar,' 30:18 — the wage-name) — written with TWO shins in all fourteen of its bare Torah tokens (and its prefixed tokens likewise, builder-checked), with ONE shin read per Ben Asher: SNAPSHOT carries the silence in the pointing itself — the first shin voweled, the second bare of any vowel — the written-two-read-one tradition instrumented letter by letter.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:20 ('זבדני אלהים אתי — the Great Scriptures' variance note is baseless: NO full אותי exists in the whole Torah except you-did-not-sanctify-ME at the end of Haazinu')
claim_en: THE ONE FULL ME: Minchat Shai's own census, computational on SNAPSHOT — the direct-object word אותי ('me') written FULL with vav appears exactly ONCE in the whole Torah: 'because you did not sanctify ME' (Deut 32:51, the waters-of-strife charge); every other token including Zebulun's dowry-verse (30:20) is lean. The dismissed variance note dies on the count.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:20 ('זבד טוב — in most books the zayin with segol, so the Radak in the Roots, six dots; and some books with five')
claim_en: THE DOWRY-WORD'S CAMP: זבד ('God has endowed me with a good ENDOWMENT,' 30:20) — the books divide six dots against five; SNAPSHOT points the zayin with tzere (the five-dot camp) against the majority segol — the run's third split-attested station, camp joined and named.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 30:20 ('הפעם — the pe with dagesh')
claim_en: THIS TIME, HARD: הפעם ('THIS TIME my husband will dwell with me,' 30:20 — Leah's sixth-son hope) — pe with dagesh (the doubling dot) as ruled, letter-identical.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 30:14 ('in all the tribe-names there is no samekh except in JOSEPH — a hint that he is the adversary of Esau — and in none an ayin except in SIMEON, for the-adulterer's-eye, from the deed of Zimri')
claim_en: THE TRIBES' TWO MARKED LETTERS (manual, builder-asserted over the eleven name-writes of this span): among all the tribe-names only JOSEPH carries a samekh and only SIMEON carries an ayin — the Kitzur reads Esau's adversary in the one and the watching eye in the other (Zimri's deed, named). Verified letter-by-letter over the naming tokens at their write-verses.
